deck: POWER IS THE SITE: START FROM AVAILABLE MEGAWATTS AND WORK BACKWARD TO LAND, FIBER, WATER AND GAS
OPTION THE DIRT, PAY FOR THE UTILITY STUDY, DISCOUNT THE QUEUE AND ORDER LONG-LEAD GEAR BEFORE THE BUILDING
site_ui.lead: Practitioners from Thor Equities, datacenterHawk, CBRE, LandBridge, Foley & Lardner and Zego show why powered land trades at 4-5x unpowered ground, why AI buyers will not look below 100 acres, and how developers lock sites through option contracts, utility studies and long-lead transformer orders while buildings wait 4-5 years for grid connection.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 171 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies on powered land, large-load interconnection, substation headroom, behind-the-meter generation and BESS site optioning for AI data centers. Every claim, metric, pro-tip and operator gate carries timestamped inline attribution back to the practitioner who said it.

flow: Call the utility and ask directly whether it can support 100MW or more, then work backward to land, fiber, water and gas at 1MW per acre with a 100-acre floor.

Pin the concept plan to a specific line such as a 230, name the redundancy source, and keep a Plan B like multifamily or a Kroger commercial deal ready before paying a $30-100k non-refundable utility study.
Tie up acreage through option contracts, from 2-3 year solar options to Stargate's $1 option, and paper each leg of a put and call on its own.
Treat announced load and queue totals skeptically; one 400MW requirement shopped by four to five developers showed up as 2GW of requests.
Place electrical orders immediately: large transformers run three to four years and grid gear two-plus years, so the building finishes long before the power does.
Budget $7-12M per MW for the build, price capacity at $100-150/kW/month, lock 10-15 year take-or-pay leases, and model the one-tenant-exit case and behind-the-meter stranding risk.
